newsitem.title: USA: ComEd 789 MW nuke to shut, seen out to June.
newsitem.headline: ComEd 789 MW nuke to shut, seen out to June.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co (ComEd) will fully shut its 789 megawatt Quad Cities nuclear power unit 2 for refueling on Friday, and expects the unit to be out of service until the end of June, a company spokesman said.
"We are going to begin a refueling outage tomorrow night," spokesman Gary Wald said, adding "they will be down to the end of June."
The unit is located in Cordova, Ill.

Power at Quad Cities 2 was reduced Wednesday while a feedwater pump was replaced, and the unit was expected to return to full power late Thursday before being shut for the refueling outage Friday, Wald said.
Quad Cities 2 was operating at 92 percent of capacity as of early Thursday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily plant status report.
The adjoining 789 megawatt Quad Cities unit 1 was operating at 72 percent of capacity early Thursday, having been reduced for a minor repair, Wald said.
Quad Cities 1 was expected to return to full service shortly, Wald said.
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
